function: Learned wideband adaptive receive beamforming: network maps low-snapshot sparse-array samples to the weights of a frequency-constrained Frost beamformer of the equivalent ULA (pp. 4-5).
system: Sparse linear minimum-redundancy arrays (4 and 7 elements), one desired signal and one interferer, 300 MHz bandwidth from 800 MHz; no RIS; no communication link modeled (pp. 5-7).
method: Complex-valued CNN (seven complex convolution layers, SE module, FC layer) trained by supervised regression with MSE loss to reproduce high-snapshot ULA beamforming weights; Adam, 300 epochs (pp. 4-7).
data_channel: Self-simulated array signals with Gaussian noise; interference angles -60 to -30 degrees in 1-degree steps, 500 samples per angle; labels from ULA weights; 7:3 train-test split (p. 5).
test_conditions: 7:3 random split of same simulated data; ideal-array training tested under position (+-0.05d) and gain/phase (+-0.5 dB, +-5 degrees) errors; separate network per array (pp. 5-9).
baselines: Classical FCFB on sparse low-snapshot data and on the ULA with high snapshots (label); learned ResNet-18, ResNet-50, MobileNetv2, MobileNetv3 applied to the same task (p. 8).
metrics: Output SINR (dB), beam patterns, training and validation MSE loss; mean side-lobe level for the covariance-reconstruction algorithm (pp. 6-10).
complexity: Symbolic FLOPs per layer of SWDBF-NN (convolution, SE, FC) versus complex multiplications of FCFB, Table VIII; stated far lower than FCFB; no runtime or parameter count (pp. 10-11).
q1_support: p. 5: "obtained through simulation" - the dataset is generated by the authors' own array-signal simulator (Gaussian noise, plane-wave signals); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "The SWDBF-NN is trained under ideal conditions" and tested with array element position errors (Table IV) and calibration errors (Table VI), conditions absent from training.
q3_support: p. 8: "ResNet-18, ResNet-50 [39], MobileNetv2 [40], and MobileNetv3 [41] in wideband beamforming tasks are presented" as learned baselines on output SINR (Table III, p. 10); p. 8: "including directly using MRA sampling data (MRA1/2-FCFB)" and ULA-FCFB are the non-learned baselines.
q4_support: p. 11: "in terms of floating point (FLOPs) operations" - per-layer FLOPs of the convolution, SE, and FC layers of SWDBF-NN against the complex multiplications of FCFB in Table VIII; the formulas are symbolic and no runtime is given.
q5_support: p. 5: "We adopt this simulation-based" approach to build the dataset; no code or data link is given, and no public dataset or measured data is used.
notes: Borderline function, included as area 3: the introduction frames the beamformer around radar array processing (p. 1) and the body never models a communication link, users, or a data rate, but the abstract states the target is massive MIMO systems and the learned network outputs beamforming weights (p. 1). Reviewer should confirm area 3 against exclusion for function. The covariance-reconstruction algorithm SWDBF-DCA is classical; only SWDBF-NN is learned. MRA2 uses a separately trained network (p. 7) and the test interference angles lie inside the training range (pp. 5, 7), so only the array-error tests count for q2.
